subtasks.title: Add scan_id + disposition to both admin Bird's Eye hit payloads
subtasks.approach: In ClarityScoutBirdsEyeController, add 'scan_id' => $hit->scan_id and 'disposition' => $hit->disposition to the payload map in BOTH hits() and recentHits(). Locate the maps BY CONTENT (the ->map(fn ($hit) => [...]) blocks projecting plate/hit_type/plate_image), NOT by the line numbers in the ticket — two prep passes disagreed on whether those drifted, so content is the only reliable anchor. In recentHits() the map ALREADY emits 'id' => $hit->id, which is the ClickHouse Hit ROW id: scan_id must be added as a SEPARATE key. Renaming or reusing 'id' would post the wrong identifier and is the single most likely way to get this node wrong. Mirror the driver payloads' key ordering and carry over the driver's DEV-2059 F1 comment intent for the disposition field (null for New Hit, else the saved string, so the control re-seeds on re-open).
subtasks.intended_diffs: ClarityScoutBirdsEyeController::hits() — add two keys to the marker payload map. ClarityScoutBirdsEyeController::recentHits() — add the same two keys alongside the existing 'id'. ClarityScoutBirdsEyeControllerTest — extend the existing recentHits assertions to pin both keys, and ADD a first-ever hits() test pinning both keys (this endpoint has no coverage today, so without it half this node ships unpinned). Cover a Staging-Live hit_type row as well as a Direct one.
subtasks.notes: This test class is CH-backed (RequiresClickhouse), so ClickHouse must be up for this node — date every hits_hot fixture relative to now(), since the hot tables enforce a 90-day TTL AT INSERT and a hardcoded date silently reads back zero rows.

subtasks.title: Add the org-scoped Bird's Eye disposition controller + POST route
subtasks.approach: Create app/Http/Controllers/Api/ClarityScoutBirdsEyeDispositionController.php as a single __invoke controller with declare(strict_types=1), modelled on ClarityScoutScanDispositionController (NOT on DispositionController — see the two defects below). Steps, in order: (1) type the parameter as the EXISTING App\Http\Requests\ScoutScanDispositionRequest — do NOT create a new FormRequest; it already restricts disposition to the driver 5 and its authorize() is just auth()->check() with no kit coupling. (2) Resolve the scan OUTSIDE any try/catch so a cross-org scan yields Laravel's clean 404 rather than being swallowed into a 500: Scan::query()->where('id', $request->input('scan_id'))->forOrg((int) auth()->user()->org_id, withSharedKits: Feature::active(FeatureEnum::SHARED_KITS->slug()))->firstOrFail(). (3) Normalize reason exactly as the driver does: $reason = $request->input('disposition') === DispositionEnum::INVALID_SCAN->value ? ($request->input('reason') ?? 'other') : 'other'. (4) Call $scan->updateDisposition(disposition: ..., user: $request->user(), reason: $reason) inside a try/catch that logs and returns 500. (5) Call Analytics::track('disposition-saved', $request->user(), ['scan_id' => ..., 'disposition' => ..., 'reason' => $reason, 'from_scout' => true], page: ScoutAnalyticsPage::BirdsEye->value) in its OWN try/catch that logs a warning and never blocks the save. Pass 'disposition-saved' as a raw string — ScoutAnalyticsEvent has no such case and both sibling controllers pass the raw string. (6) Return response(status: 200). Then register the route in routes/web.php inside the scout/org-map Route::prefix('api') group, grouped with the explicit routes and above the GET-only {any} JSON-404 catch-all: Route::post('scan/disposition', ClarityScoutBirdsEyeDispositionController::class)->middleware('throttle:30,1');
subtasks.intended_diffs: One new controller file. One added route line in routes/web.php. One new Postgres-only test class (NOT RequiresClickhouse, matching the repo convention that routing/write-path tests run in normal CI) mirroring DispositionControllerTest's org-scoping conventions and ClarityScoutScanDispositionControllerTest's analytics/activity conventions.
must_pin_in_tests: Admin CAN disposition a scan on ANY kit in their own org (not only a kit they drove) — the whole point of org- vs kit-scoping.

Cross-org scan returns 404, NOT 500. This is a derived AC: DispositionController's swallow-to-500 is pinned by its own test, and reusing it would have made an authorization failure indistinguishable from a server error.

A non-Invalid-Scan disposition posted with NO reason key creates NO scan_validations row. This is the derived AC guarding the verified defect: map.js omits reason unless truthy, and Scan::updateDisposition's guard `if ($reason !== 'other')` is satisfied by null, so an unnormalized reason would spam the human-review queue on every Accessible/New Hit/Moving/Inaccessible save.
Invalid Scan WITH a real reason still DOES create a scan_validations row (proves the normalization did not over-correct).
activity('Disposition') is attributed to the ADMIN user.
Analytics 'disposition-saved' fires with from_scout=true AND page='clarity-scout-birds-eye' (the Q1 decision).
An admin-only enum value (Valid / Reviewed / Invalid) is rejected 422 (the Q2 decision).
Nonexistent scan_id returns 404; missing/invalid disposition returns 422.
Middleware gating: a non-admin is refused, and an org without the CLARITY_SCOUT feature is refused.
subtasks.notes: The route addition and the controller are one node deliberately: a route pointing at a nonexistent controller class does not boot, so splitting them would leave an intermediate broken state.

subtasks.title: Switch admin hits() + recentHits() to actionableDisposition() (AC-2 driver parity)
subtasks.approach: In ClarityScoutBirdsEyeController, change the disposition filter on hits() (~line 305) and recentHits() (~line 559) from ->validDisposition() to ->actionableDisposition(). LEAVE stats() (~line 494) on validDisposition() — the driver deliberately keeps the analytics rule there and both controllers' comments say so. Use actionableDisposition(), NOT liveActionable(): the admin surfaces intentionally include Staging_Live via forHitTypes([Live, Staging_Live]), and liveActionable() would force hit_type=Live and drop Staging hits.
subtasks.intended_diffs: Two scope-call changes + tests pinning that an Accessible-dispositioned hit is RETAINED by both admin surfaces (and that stats() still excludes it).
subtasks.origin: NOT in the original plan. blast_radius_summary: No subtask carries a blast-radius tag. Checked against the sensitive globs: no database/migrations/** change, no billing job or resource, no Shield/Policy/auth-config file, no Clickhouse*Purge|Cleanup, no PruneScans. The change IS tenancy-relevant (a new authenticated org-scoped write endpoint), which is why t2 is classified complex and why review lane selection must escalate — but it does not match the sensitive globs, so no pre-approval line is required before Phase 4.
review_hint: Phase 5 must escalate to --lanes=3: the diff is squarely in semantic-correctness territory (org tenancy on a new write path, plus the reason-normalization guard whose failure mode is silent human-review-queue pollution rather than an error). t4 changes a READ surface, so the review must also check that stats() was left on validDisposition() and that Staging_Live hits are not dropped.
